title: Generalized Federated Learning via Sharpness Aware Minimization
publication_status_observed: ICML 2022 (Proceedings of the 39th International Conference on Machine Learning, Baltimore, Maryland, USA, PMLR 162, 2022)
main_claims: Using SAM as the local optimizer in federated learning (FedSAM) improves the generalization of the global model and reduces performance deviation across clients under non-IID data distributions.
MoFedSAM, which additionally incorporates global model momentum into local SAM training, achieves faster convergence and better performance than FedSAM.
FedSAM and MoFedSAM achieve convergence rates matching the best existing FL algorithms while providing generalization guarantees.
methodology: FedSAM replaces the standard SGD local optimizer in FedAvg with SAM, where each client applies a two-step SAM update using its local data. MoFedSAM additionally downloads the previous global model update and incorporates it into local SAM training. Convergence is proved under standard FL assumptions (L-smooth loss, bounded gradient variance). Empirical evaluation compares FedSAM and MoFedSAM against FedAvg, FedProx, SCAFFOLD, and other FL baselines on image classification tasks with non-IID data splits.
key_results: FedSAM convergence rate: O(L*F / sqrt(R*K*N)) for full client participation, matching the best existing FL convergence rates.
MoFedSAM achieves speedup with convergence rate O(sqrt(beta)*L / sqrt(R*K*N)), outperforming FedSAM in experiments.
FedSAM and MoFedSAM substantially outperform existing FL algorithms including FedAvg, FedProx, SCAFFOLD on non-IID benchmarks in terms of accuracy and reduced performance deviation.
limitations: The convergence analysis requires assumptions (bounded gradient variance, L-smoothness) that may not tightly hold for heterogeneous real-world FL data.
The method requires double the computation per local step due to SAM's two-pass structure, increasing communication and compute overhead in FL settings.
Experiments are limited in scale and dataset diversity; generalization to very large models or diverse FL environments is not demonstrated.
relevance_to_rq: Peripheral relevance: FedSAM applies SAM to federated/distributed learning with non-IID data (a form of distribution shift), which relates to the sam_mechanism sub-topic by demonstrating SAM's flat minima benefit under heterogeneous data. However, the federated learning context is substantially different from the single-model CIFAR-C OOD setting of the RQ.
